title: Analysis of Sugars, Organic Acids, and Alcohols by HPLC-RID
author: Hannah M. Alt
materials: Instrument equilibration Purge instrument with 0.01 N sulfuric acid solution made in the previous step. Be certain the instrument is purged through the entire flow path including the detector, before the analytical column is plumbed in. The Aminex 87H column is sensitive to solvents, for example, a higher amount of methanol will damage the column. The purge step is needed to remove all solvents/mobile phases from the analytical system. (See Bio-Rad's ' Instruction Manual ' for Aminex resin-based columns for solvent compatibility and installation details). Add the guard column and analytical column to the system and begin equilibrating the column at a low flow rate of 0.2 mL/min while the column reaches analysis temperature. During the column equilibration, begin purging the reference cell of the refractive index detector (RID), this process will continue through the final equilibration of the column. At intervals of at least 10 minutes, increase the flow by 0.2 mL/min until you reach the method flow of 0.6 mL/min. Once the column is up to method flow and both the column compartment and the RID are at method temperature and stable, the RID reference cell can be closed. This typically takes around 30 minutes after method flow is reached. A longer purge of the reference cell is not detrimental. After the reference cell is closed, wait for the RID signal to stabilize before starting analysis.

Standards Allow standard level ampules (listed in 'Materials' section) to come to room temperature, vortex, and transfer contents of ampules into 2 mL amber HPLC vials. To create lower concentration calibration levels than provided in the kit, dilute the lowest concentration ampule to your desired concentration. Example calibration concentration table created from commercial standards 'Carboxylic Acids Standards Kit' by Absolute Standards referenced in 'Materials'. Notice the calibration range was extended to lower concentrations by diluting "level 1" by 2x, 5x, and 10x, respectively. Calibration verification standard (CVS) level is a commercial quality control level described in section 6.2. (Click to enlarge) Reporting limits and linear ranges may vary and should be determined for each instrument individually. The standard ranges provided by the manufacturer are suggested starting amounts and may change depending on instrument response.

steps.title: Configure HPLC system
steps.instruction: Install an Aminex HPX‑87H column (300 × 8.7 mm, 9 µm) on an Agilent 1200 Series HPLC, set the column and RID oven to 55 °C, program an isocratic flow of 0.01 N (0.005 M) sulfuric acid at 0.6 mL/min, and set the injection volume to 6.0 µL (optional increase to 20 µL for lower detection limit, noting possible upper‑limit reduction).

substeps.instruction: Mount the HPX‑87H column according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Set column oven temperature to 55 °C.
Set RID detector temperature to 55 °C.
Program the HPLC method: isocratic 0.01 N H₂SO₄, flow = 0.6 mL/min, run time = 27 min.
Set injection volume to 6.0 µL (or up to 20 µL if a lower reporting limit is required).

steps.title: Prepare 0.01 N sulfuric acid mobile phase
steps.instruction: Dilute 1.0 mL of 10 N sulfuric acid into 1.0 L of 18.2 MΩ·cm ultrapure water to obtain 0.01 N (0.005 M) sulfuric acid, and make enough volume for the entire sequence (≈18.0 mL per injection).

substeps.instruction: Measure 1.0 mL of 10 N H₂SO₄ with a calibrated pipette.
Add the acid to a volumetric flask containing ~900 mL ultrapure water.
Mix and dilute to the final volume of 1.0 L with ultrapure water.
Transfer the solution to a clean, airtight container and label it.
Calculate total volume needed (number of injections × 18.0 mL) and prepare that amount before starting the run.

steps.title: Generate calibration curves
steps.instruction: Prepare a series of standard solutions covering the expected concentration range, inject each, and construct linear calibration curves for each analyte ensuring a correlation coefficient (r²) ≥ 0.995 using a fit that ignores the origin.

substeps.instruction: Prepare at least five standard concentrations for each target analyte.
Inject each standard under the HPLC conditions defined in Step 1.
Record peak areas and plot area versus concentration.
Perform linear regression without forcing the line through the origin.
Confirm that r² ≥ 0.995 for every analyte; repeat standards if any curve fails.

steps.title: Prepare calibration verification standards (CVS)
steps.instruction: Obtain the manufacturer‑provided CVS level, and re‑analyze it at least every 20 samples to verify instrument drift, accepting recoveries within ±10 % of the expected amount.

substeps.instruction: Aliquot the CVS solution into individual vials.
Inject the CVS after every ≤20 sample injections.
Calculate the measured concentration versus the certified value.
Accept the run if recovery is between 90 % and 110 %; otherwise troubleshoot the instrument.

steps.title: Prepare samples for injection
steps.instruction: Filter each sample through a 0.2 µm (or smaller) filter appropriate for the matrix, and dilute any sample anticipated to exceed the linear range to keep concentrations within the calibrated limits.

substeps.instruction: Select the filter type and part number specified for the sample matrix.
Pass the sample through the filter into a clean vial.
If necessary, dilute the filtered sample with the 0.01 N sulfuric acid mobile phase to fall within the calibration range.
Mix gently and label the vial for injection.

steps.title: Run HPLC analysis
steps.instruction: Inject each prepared sample (6.0 µL or up to 20 µL if needed) sequentially, monitoring the run time of 27 minutes per injection, and note any co‑eluting peaks (ethanol, butyric acid, xylose, galactose, mannose, fructose).

substeps.instruction: Load the sample vials onto the autosampler.
Start the sequence, ensuring the system uses the mobile phase prepared in Step 2.
Observe chromatograms for the expected retention times; run single‑analyte markers if retention times are uncertain.
Collect peak area data for each analyte.

steps.title: Evaluate data and verify performance
steps.instruction: Compare sample concentrations to calibration curves, confirm that CVS recoveries remain within ±10 %, and assess any co‑eluting peaks; repeat injections or adjust injection volume if signal saturation or poor quantitation occurs.

substeps.instruction: Calculate concentrations using the calibration equations.
Check that all sample results fall within the linear range.
Review CVS results; if out of the 90‑110 % window, re‑calibrate or troubleshoot.
If peaks are overlapping, consider running individual analyte markers or adjusting injection volume.
